Ompok pinnatus Ng, H.H., 2003. Common name: Long-fin Glass Catfish. Type locality: Cambodia: Tonle Sap at Kompong Chhnang. Size: 81 mm (3.2") SL. IUCN Red List status: Data Deficient.

The genus Ompok consists of medium-sized silurid fishes found in inland waters throughout South and Southeast Asia. It is traditionally diagnosed by a short dorsal fin with 4 rays, a strongly forked caudal fin, a subcutaneous eye set immediately posterior to the mouth rictus and two patches of palatal teeth (Weber & de Beaufort, 1913). Bornbusch (1995) showed that Ompok, as currently understood, is probably paraphyletic.

Like O. eugeneiatus, it is easily distinguished from congeners by the very long barbels. Ompok pinnatus differs from O. eugeneiatus in having a deeper caudal peduncle, shorter mandibular barbels and fewer anal-fin rays.
Southeast Asia: Chao Phraya and Mekong River drainages in Thailand and Cambodia.
Provide hiding spaces in the form of driftwood or PVC pipes as well as plenty of vegetation. Prefers an area of open water when active.
Readily feeds on live or frozen foods and other prepared foods such as pellets. May eat very small fishes.
A relatively peaceful species that is compatible with most fish. Not safe with very small fishes.
Males are more slender and have strong serrations on the posterior edge of the pectoral spine (females lack these serrations).
Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington v. 116 (no. 1), pp 48, Fig. 1.
